_comment: The supplier lines for the September 2026 batch, transcribed verbatim from the owner.
Costs are IQD, per variant, exactly as given — nothing here is computed or rounded.
`account` is null where the owner did not state one; those are not guessed.
Selling prices are NOT in this file. Cost is what the supplier charges and is a fact;
price is a decision, and it is recorded per product so a change to it is reviewable.

rules.note: Owner's rules for this batch. The shared engine's switch1 band is 5,000-15,000 and its online uplift is a multiplier that yields under 10,000 profit on most of these lines; neither is edited, because that would reprice the existing catalogue.

pricing.offline: round250(5000 + 13000 * position[tier]), lifted clear of cost when the band would price at or under it. position: flagship 1, major 0.65, standard 0.35, niche 0.12.
pricing.online: round250(cost + 10000 + demandBonus[tier]). A floor of 10,000 profit, widened by demand — not a multiplier on cost, which would pay least on the cheapest lines and most on the dearest regardless of how well the game sells.
pricing.fourOption: Two offline and two online. The dearer of each pair is priced above the cheaper by the difference in what they cost to acquire, so the ladder reflects the content.

games._ambiguous: needs_identity_review. Same Chinese name as n=20 (Onimusha: Warlords) but a four-rung ladder: Regular 1,540 / Deluxe 6,380 / Complete 26,180 / Ultimate 42,680. Capcom's only current four-edition Onimusha is Way of the Sword, whose tiers are Standard / Deluxe / Premium Deluxe — no Complete and no Ultimate — and that is n=23 already, on Switch 2. No Onimusha title on Nintendo matches this ladder, so which game it is cannot be proven and nothing is created for it.
